investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T21:48:46–50Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval org has reached or exceeded the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks (evidenced by the runner calling createAgent at run-status-probes.mjs:1339 immediately after requireOrgId), none of the checks can proceed past this gate, producing a total evidence blackout and a full feature failure. This is an eval-infrastructure / production-API resource-limit failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact is not confirmed by this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T21:48:46–50Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval org has reached or exceeded the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks (evidenced by the runner calling createAgent at run-status-probes.mjs:1339 immediately after requireOrgId), none of the checks can proceed past this gate, producing a total evidence blackout and a full feature failure. This is an eval-infrastructure / production-API resource-limit failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact is not confirmed by this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary – Eval org agent quota exhausted: the swarm service enforces a hard limit of 100 agents per org; the eval org has accumulated agents from prior runs (possibly due to incomplete cleanup) and has hit that ceiling, causing every new POST /api/agents to be rejected.
Secondary – Cleanup (withCleanup / track) failed in a prior eval run, leaving orphaned remote agents that count against the quota without being deleted.

Tertiary – The quota limit itself was recently lowered or the eval org was reassigned to a tier with a lower limit, causing previously-passing runs to now exceed the cap (no historical pass data is available to confirm regression: verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0).

investigations.rootCause: The production-api runtime environment is unreachable or misconfigured for the agent session endpoint targeted by the image-generation-stream eval. The SSE stream to /api/generate/image/stream opened successfully (generation_start received), but the subsequent agent session open call returned HTTP 404, causing a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame and aborting the stream before any generation_completed frame or image artifact URL could be produced. This is an eval-infrastructure or deployment configuration failure scoped to the production-api runtime; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so a user-facing outage cannot be asserted.
